property_summary: Calling allowance does not change the wards mapping for any address.
The wards mapping is unchanged after calling allowance.
Calling allowance with the caller being a ward does not change the wards mapping for that caller.
After calling allowance, the wards mapping value for address(this) remains 1.
The caller's wards entry remains 1 after calling allowance.
After any sequence of calls ending with allowance, the wards mapping is unchanged for any address that was never relied or denied.
After any sequence of calls ending with allowance, wards[user] remains 1 if deny(user) was called before, because deny should set wards[user] = 0 but the bug sets it to 1.
After any call to allowance, the wards mapping is unchanged for any address that was never relied or denied (i.e., never had wards set to 1).
After calling deny(user) on the reference C, wards[user] is always 0, but on the buggy version it is 1, observable through the public getter wards(user).
After any sequence of calls, calling deny(user) sets wards[user] to 0 for the reference, but the bug sets it to 1.
The allowance getter of C always returns the allowance from the share token contract, and does not modify the wards mapping.
The wards mapping for any address remains the same before and after a call to allowance.
The allowance function does not modify the wards mapping, so wards[caller] should always equal the initial value set in the constructor for an address that was never explicitly granted authorization.
Calling allowance with any two addresses does not change the wards mapping for the caller.
The wards mapping for any address is not changed by calling allowance on the contract.
After any call to allowance, the value of wards[msg.sender] should remain unchanged if the caller was not previously authorized (i.e., wards[caller] == 0).
After calling allowance(address,address), the return value should be a boolean true if the caller was previously authorized (wards[caller] == 1), otherwise it should revert.
After a successful call to allowance, if wards[caller] was 0 then the caller cannot later call rely on any address.
Calling allowance does not change the caller's authorization status (wards[msg.sender] must remain equal to its value before the call).
The value of wards[msg.sender] is never changed by calling allowance with any arguments.
After calling allowance, the caller must be authorized (wards[caller] == 1).
After any public call, wards[caller] remains 1 if caller was authorized before, and the allowance return value from the share contract is unchanged.
After calling allowance with any arguments, the caller's authorization status (wards[caller]) must remain unchanged (either 0 or 1).
After calling allowance with any arguments, the caller's authorization status (wards[caller]) must remain unchanged (either 0 or 1).
Calling allowance (any arguments) does not change the caller's authorization status (wards[caller]).
After calling allowance(address,address) with the zero address as both arguments, the contract state (as reflected by the return value of allowance) should be the same as before the call.
After calling allowance with the same address as both arguments, the return value equals the share contract's allowance for those addresses.
Running allowance with the same msg.sender as both arguments never changes the wards mapping status of msg.sender from 1 to 0.
Calling allowance with any valid addresses does not change the wards mapping for address(0).
Calling allowance with the same address as both arguments should not change the caller's authorization status from authorized to unauthorized.
After allowing any user to call deny(), the value of wards[msg.sender] becomes 0, so a subsequent auth-guarded call fails.
After any call to allowance(address,address), the caller's wards entry remains 1 (authorized).
After any call to allowance(address,address), the wards[msg.sender] of the contract remains 1 (authorized).
Calling allowance(address,address) leaves wards[cutie] unchanged for any previously authorized caller cutie.
The allowance function does not change the wards mapping for any address.
The auth modifier should never revert when the caller is authorized.
The allowance function should never revert for any owner and spender addresses.
allowance always returns a uint256 and never reverts for any addresses
The allowance function always returns the share token's allowance for any owner and spender, regardless of the caller's authorization status.
The allowance function does not revert for any owner and spender addresses.
The value of latestPrice is unchanged by a call to allowance.
After calling allowance, latestPrice equals its value before the call, regardless of the address arguments.
The state variable latestPrice is not modified by a call to allowance with any arguments.
After calling allowance, the state variable latestPrice remains equal to the value it had immediately before the call.
Calling allowance does not change the value of latestPrice.
After calling allowance(address,address), the state variable latestPrice is unchanged from before the call.
After any sequence of public calls ending with allowance(address,address), the value of latestPrice remains the same as before the call.
After calling allowance(address,address), the value of latestPrice is equal to the value recorded at lastPriceUpdate (i.e., the stored price should not be zero unless it was explicitly set to zero).
After calling allowance(address,address), the value of latestPrice should be identical to the value recorded at the time of lastPriceUpdate.
Calling allowance does not change latestPrice
After any sequence of public function calls ending with allowance, the lastPriceUpdate state variable remains unchanged.
The allowance function should never modify the lastPriceUpdate state variable.
Calling allowance on the contract does not change lastPriceUpdate.
Calling allowance does not change the value of lastPriceUpdate.
The value of lastPriceUpdate is always zero (0) because it is never updated in the buggy version.
After any call to allowance(address,address) with any arguments, the return value of totalAssets() must be unaffected (i.e., remain the same as before the call).
After a call to allowance(address,address), the value of c.latestPrice() must remain unchanged.
After any call to allowance(address,address), the state variable c.lastPriceUpdate() must remain unchanged.
After calling allowance with arbitrary addresses, the value of c.asset() must remain the same as before the call.
After any call to allowance(address,address), the return value of totalSupply() must remain unchanged.
totalAssets returns the same value as investmentManager.totalAssets(totalSupply(), address(this)).
totalAssets returns the same value as investmentManager.totalAssets(totalSupply(), address(this)).
The result of c.totalSupply() is less than or equal to the result of c.totalAssets() when called directly.
totalAssets() returns a value that is greater than or equal to investmentManager.totalAssets(c.totalSupply(), address(this)) when totalSupply() > 0.
For any address a, the value returned by c.totalAssets() equals investmentManager.totalAssets(c.totalSupply(), address(c)).
totalAssets() must be consistent with convertToAssets(totalSupply()) plus any invariant from the investment manager.
For any address a, b, allowance(a, b) must be less than or equal to share.allowance(a, b) when the call succeeds.
totalAssets() should return a value that, when passed to convertToAssets, yields a value <= the original assets plus a small rounding error.
totalAssets() must be consistent with the share's totalSupply and the return value of convertToShares should be bounded by the totalAssets.
For any address owner, the value returned by allowance(owner, address(0)) must be less than or equal to share.allowance(owner, address(0)) when the call succeeds.
